newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi to visit Germany on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Prodi to visit Germany on Monday.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi will visit Germany on Monday to meet the prime minister of Bavaria, Edmund Stoiber, and senior German business leaders, Stoiber's office said on Thursday.
Prodi will meet Stoiber for a working lunch in Munich at 1030 GMT and will hold a news conference at 1245 GMT.

He will then travel to Frankfurt where he is scheduled to hold a news conference at 1530 GMT or 1600 GMT and meet leading German business representatives at a dinner hosted by Commerzbank AG, the bank said.

Prodi's visit, which follows a state visit to Bonn only last week, comes amid speculation that Germany does not want Italy in Europe's planned monetary union from the start because its membership may weaken the euro.

Last week, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl reassured Prodi he had no objections to Italy's joining the single currency and dismissed reports of a scheme to keep Rome out of the starting line-up for the euro, scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999.

But senior German bankers have recently warned of turmoil on financial markets if Mediterranean countries like Italy, whose currencies have been less stable than the mark, were allowed to help launch the euro.
Meanwhile Stoiber, one of Germany's staunchest advocates of a rock-hard single currency, has voiced doubts about Italy's ability to fulfill the stability criteria strictly.

In a television interview earlier this month, Stoiber said that accepting creative accounting to allow countries to join economic and monetary union meant that "we'll never succeed in having the Italians and the Spanish and the Portuguese (keep to) a strict application of the stability criteria."
